summary: Session titles now come from spec.md on every surface, and one writer owns session-state.json. The extension's buildSessions hardcoded `Session ${n}` in a module that had already computed the spec's title map, and because title resolution puts the stored ledger first, whichever writer reached disk first made that label permanent — 130 rows across this repo carried it. One shared pure rule (progress.heal_title / healTitle) now resolves titles: a spec heading beats a generic-shaped stored title, an operator-authored title is never overwritten. It runs at the writer so the fix persists, and in the read view so closed sets — which get no further boundary write — display correctly without a migration script rewriting their records; the reader's spec read is conditional, so a healthy set costs no extra disk read. Ownership is settled by removal: the extension's readStatus no longer writes, ensureSessionStateFile is deleted, and readSessionSets consumes an in-memory derivation, so a scan can no longer race the router's writer or drop an untracked file into the operator's tree. A 14-case corpus, asserted by both languages, pins the rule shut. Verification (2 discovery lenses + supplementary) found 3 Major defects — 4 spec.md reads per spec-only set per scan, and an empty activity-log parity gap the extension had never mirrored from Set 077 S4 — both remediated with read-counting and per-shape falsifiers; remediation-review returned VERIFIED with 2 fix-accepted verdicts.

reason.specifics: Session 2 (left-click a session, land on its plan) works the same surface this session just restructured — readSessionSets' row model, the session ledger, and the new optional specTitles threading — so continuity of that context is worth more than a fresh perspective. No blocker, no cost pressure, no capability gap; verification stays cross-provider regardless.
